external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser outside the system's network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.
external_entities.notes: The browser sits outside our network.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application receives browser traffic, enqueues jobs, and reads its configuration.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue
processes.notes: The web application has queue credentials in its config store.

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: The background worker picks up jobs, does the work, and reads and writes the database.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.
processes.notes: The worker has database credentials in its config store.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue holding jobs for the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used for application log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: A config store containing the web application's settings and queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config
data_stores.notes: The config store holds the web application's queue credentials.

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: A config store containing the worker's settings and database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config
data_stores.notes: The config store holds the worker's database credentials.

data_flows.name: browser traffic
data_flows.description: Traffic from the user's browser to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: enqueue jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue

data_flows.name: pick up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up

data_flows.name: read and write records
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database, including application log records.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.data_description: database records and application log records

data_flows.name: read settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from the web application config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config
data_flows.notes: The settings include the web application's queue credentials.

data_flows.name: read settings
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from the worker config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: ... the worker has a worker config.
data_flows.notes: The settings include the worker's database credentials.

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet zone outside the system's network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: over HTTP/S across the public internet

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The network tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier containing the queue, worker, database, and config stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is reachable from the internet because a user's browser talks to it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that a user's browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is described as a background worker process rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a background worker process that picks up jobs and does work.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential because it holds the web application's queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds the worker's database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds database credentials.
